provenance.semanticBasis: Dexter required every execution deviation, whether self-found or reported by Dexter, to be root-caused and recorded in project memory before continuing.

genericProblem: An execution can drift from repository constraints when the agent responds to a problem from local intuition instead of first reopening AGENTS.md, the routed project memory, and the applicable design/evidence package; correcting the immediate action without recording that retrieval failure does not reduce recurrence.

finiteDenominator.selector: runtime and verification execution-boundary decisions in the RM1 P6-3 task
finiteDenominator.finding: The deviation was not the absence of a remote runner: the repository already had one. Its root cause was acting on the runtime problem from local intuition before reopening AGENTS.md, routed project memory, and the managed-runtime skill/source package; that retrieval omission then led to an invalid local Docker/Colima attempt.

finiteDenominator.selector: compile proof after controller source change
finiteDenominator.finding: The controller was changed to bind a generated enum but the generated type import was not verified before the first remote L2 attempt.

finiteDenominator.selector: UI control-level IA admission before any P6-3 dynamic proof
finiteDenominator.finding: A backend remote Testcontainers proof was started while the U03 control-level final alignment record remained PENDING; the runner path proves backend behavior and cleanup only, but the execution sequence did not first establish and mechanically distinguish the required UI IA conformance gate.

finiteDenominator.selector: shell loops that issue compliance receipts during RM1 P6-3 implementation
finiteDenominator.finding: A local shell variable named PATH overwrote the process command lookup while recording source-read receipts. The intended receipts were not created; no repository byte changed. The root cause was using a reserved execution-environment variable as local loop state instead of an intent-specific variable name.

finiteDenominator.selector: standards coverage invocation for the active RM1 P6-3 package
finiteDenominator.finding: The check was initially invoked with the Roadmap CURRENT_STEP token RM1-P6-3 rather than the active package's explicit standardsPhase R5. The UNKNOWN_PHASE result was not a standards failure: the root cause was again skipping the governing package input and guessing an execution parameter from the Roadmap label.

finiteDenominator.selector: backend focused-proof entry for the active P6-3 owner/edge change
finiteDenominator.finding: The first focused-proof command guessed a repository-root ./gradlew wrapper and failed before a test ran. The repository instead declares the remote managed Testcontainers entry in scripts/README.md. The root cause was selecting a conventional local command before reopening the governing script and package verification boundary.

searchQueries: rg remote managed runner local Docker Colima scripts/test
read active package input standardsPhase before standards-coverage
read scripts/README.md and active package before backend focused proof

counterexamples.reason: The repository already provides the required remote Docker/Testcontainers execution path; local runtime setup is not a valid substitute.
Reading the governing source is necessary but does not itself prove that a deviation was root-caused and persisted for future prevention.

findings.genericProblem: The governing-source recall step was skipped before diagnosing and selecting a runtime path.
findings.minimalRepair: When any problem or deviation appears, first reopen AGENTS.md, the routed project-memory hits, the owning design/evidence sources, and the applicable local skill; then identify the violated boundary and root cause, document the finite denominator and counterexamples, and persist the reusable rule in project memory before the next implementation or test action.

findings.genericProblem: A production source change entered remote L2 without a local or focused compile proof for its imported generated symbols.
findings.minimalRepair: After each source change, run the smallest available static compile/typecheck proof for the changed production boundary before remote L2; treat compiler output as a first-failure diagnostic and do not proceed while imports or generated symbols are unresolved.

findings.genericProblem: A focused test edit was structurally misplaced and entered remote L2 without compiling the exact test source first.
findings.minimalRepair: When a focused proof is changed, reopen the changed test and its owning production source, run the narrowest available test compilation or equivalent parser/typecheck before remote L2, and verify each new fixture variable is scoped to the test that owns it.

findings.genericProblem: A dynamic proof route can be mistaken for the UI L2 gate when control-level UI IA alignment is still pending.
findings.minimalRepair: Keep backend owner proof explicitly typed as backend evidence; before any UI-bearing P6-3 L2, require a PASS control-level alignment record for the complete admitted UI denominator and record the distinction in package evidence.

findings.genericProblem: A receipt or verification command can be silently skipped when shell loop state shadows a reserved environment variable.
findings.minimalRepair: Use descriptive non-reserved local names such as targetPath; after every receipt loop, require and inspect one PASS line per expected source before treating the write admission as satisfied.

findings.genericProblem: A managed verification can be invoked with a guessed Roadmap token instead of the package-owned parameter that defines its valid vocabulary.
findings.minimalRepair: Before any package-required command, reopen its active package input and pass its explicit parameter value; treat an unknown-parameter response as a first-failure diagnostic, then identify the owning source instead of trying additional guessed values.

findings.genericProblem: A build or test can start from a guessed local entrypoint instead of the repository-managed command and its approved verification stage.
findings.minimalRepair: Before every managed proof, reopen scripts/README.md, the active package and the applicable local skill; select the declared entrypoint and verify that its phase is currently admitted before invocation.

preventionDispositions.reason: The user-requested discipline becomes a durable execution constraint and requires root-cause memory persistence rather than a one-turn correction.

preventionDispositions.owningSourceOrControl: P6 implementation focused-proof checklist: changed production boundary compile before managed L2
preventionDispositions.reason: The remote runner is for managed runtime proof; unresolved generated imports must be caught by the cheaper focused compile gate first.

preventionDispositions.owningSourceOrControl: P6 implementation focused-proof checklist: changed focused test compile before managed L2
preventionDispositions.reason: A changed focused test must compile in isolation before any managed runtime evidence is attempted.
The control-level IA record and backend dynamic evidence remain separate; a backend PASS cannot authorize or substitute for UI L2.
The failure is a reusable execution discipline; command output must confirm receipt completion rather than assuming a loop ran.
The active package owns verification parameters that may intentionally differ from Roadmap status vocabulary; this must be recovered before command execution.
The repository scripts, not common local tool conventions, own the permitted dynamic proof entrypoint and stage.
